newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday on a technical correction after sharp gains in the past two weeks, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,590 yuan ($2,845) per tonne, losing 180 yuan. It opened at 23,650 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,550 and a high of 23,710.
March fell 150 to 23,250, April 180 to 23,440, May 130 to 23,590 and July 150 to 23,590.
Combined volume fell to 32,840 tonnes from 37,730.
Traders said some investors liquidated long positions after Friday's poor performance on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
"Some wary investors began to liquidate on concerns of possible falls over the next few days," one trader said.
"The LME's strong upward trend seems to have slowed and that discouraged long position holders in Shanghai," he added.
Some traders said that current high spot copper prices could not support futures prices in the long term.
"The average spot price for the whole year can not stay at such high levels because of global oversupply," a second trader said. "So producers are likely to hedge in the futures markets."
But sharp falls seemed unlikely as investors were willing to buy on corrections, traders said. Analysts expected copper to move in a narrow range in the short term.
Aluminium ended up. March rose 100 16,000 yuan ($1,928) per tonne, April 150 to 16,350, May 100 to 16,700 and June 100 to 16,900. Combined volume rose to 5,380 tonnes from 2,010.
